title: Retention Call Procedure — Standard Operating Procedure
content:
RETENTION CALL PROCEDURE
========================

Purpose: Guide service representatives through retention calls for at-risk customers.

STEP 1 — PREPARATION
Review the customer's 360 profile before calling. Note:
- Active policies and renewal dates
- Recent interaction history and sentiment
- Risk tier and contributing signals
- NBA recommendation and confidence level

STEP 2 — OPENING
Acknowledge the customer by name. Reference their tenure. Express appreciation for their loyalty.

STEP 3 — LISTEN AND ACKNOWLEDGE
Ask open-ended questions about their experience. Listen actively. Acknowledge any frustrations without being defensive. Document key concerns.

STEP 4 — OFFER SOLUTIONS
Based on the customer's concerns and the NBA recommendation:
- For premium concerns: Review discount eligibility, multi-policy bundles, deductible adjustments
- For service complaints: Offer dedicated representative, escalate unresolved issues, provide direct contact
- For coverage questions: Schedule a coverage review, explain current protections

STEP 5 — CLOSE AND FOLLOW-UP
Summarize actions taken. Set clear expectations for next steps. Schedule follow-up if needed. Log the interaction and decision in the system.

IMPORTANT: All retention offers must be approved through the human review gate. Do not promise discounts without supervisor authorization.

title: Complaint Escalation Procedure
content:
COMPLAINT ESCALATION PROCEDURE
===============================

When to escalate:
- Customer has called 3+ times about the same issue
- Complaint involves a regulatory concern
- Customer threatens to file a DOI complaint
- Issue has been unresolved for more than 15 business days
- Customer requests a supervisor

ESCALATION LEVELS
-----------------
Level 1 — Senior Representative: Handle complex policy or billing disputes. Response within 24 hours.
Level 2 — Team Supervisor: Handle unresolved Level 1 issues, authorization for retention offers >10%. Response within 4 hours.
Level 3 — Department Manager: Handle regulatory threats, legal concerns, high-value customer retention. Response within 2 hours.

DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
- Log all escalation details in the interaction record
- Include: original complaint date, number of prior contacts, customer sentiment, specific request, and resolution attempted
- Attach evidence from the customer's 360 profile

RESOLUTION TRACKING
- All escalated complaints must be resolved within 5 business days
- Send confirmation to customer when resolved
- Log resolution in decision audit trail

title: Cross-Sell Eligibility Rules and Guidelines
content:
CROSS-SELL ELIGIBILITY RULES
============================

Eligible cross-sell opportunities are identified by the NBA engine based on customer profile analysis. Representatives should follow these guidelines:

AUTO → HOME BUNDLE
- Eligible if: customer has auto policy, no home policy, tenure > 1 year, payment history is good
- Discount: 10-15% multi-policy discount on combined premium
- Timing: Best during renewal window or after positive interaction

HOME → UMBRELLA
- Eligible if: customer has home policy with dwelling limit > $300K, no umbrella policy
- Discount: 5% umbrella discount when bundled
- Timing: During coverage review or after claim settlement

AUTO → RENTERS (for non-homeowners)
- Eligible if: customer has auto only, no home policy, address indicates rental
- Discount: 8% bundle discount

DO NOT CROSS-SELL WHEN:
- Customer has open complaint (wait until resolved)
- Risk tier is critical (focus on retention first)
- Customer sentiment is negative in last 30 days
- Customer has explicitly declined in last 6 months

title: Renewal Discount Policy and Authorization Matrix
content:
RENEWAL DISCOUNT POLICY
=======================

Purpose: Define authorized discount levels for policy renewals to support customer retention.

STANDARD DISCOUNTS (no approval required):
- Multi-policy bundle: 10-15% (auto-applied)
- Claims-free 3+ years: 5%
- Loyalty 5+ years: 3%
- Paperless billing: 2%
- Autopay enrollment: 2%

RETENTION DISCOUNTS (supervisor approval required):
- At-risk customer adjustment: up to 10%
- Competitive match: up to 12% (requires competitor quote)
- Win-back offer: up to 15% (lapsed customer returning)

MAXIMUM COMBINED DISCOUNT: 25%

AUTHORIZATION MATRIX:
- Up to 10%: Service representative (standard discounts only)
- 10-15%: Team supervisor approval
- 15-20%: Department manager approval
- 20-25%: VP approval (exceptional cases only)

All discounts must be logged in the decision audit trail with justification and approver information.

title: Claim Filing and Processing Guide for Representatives
content:
CLAIM FILING AND PROCESSING GUIDE
=================================

STEP 1 — INTAKE
Collect the following from the customer:
- Policy number and customer ID
- Date and time of loss
- Description of the incident
- Police report number (if applicable)
- Photos or documentation (if available)
- Contact information for other parties involved

STEP 2 — VERIFICATION
- Verify policy is active and covers the type of loss
- Check deductible amount for applicable coverage
- Confirm no duplicate claim exists
- Review coverage limits

STEP 3 — ASSIGNMENT
- Auto claims < $5,000: Fast-track processing (5 business days)
- Auto claims $5,000-$25,000: Standard adjuster assignment
- Home claims: Field inspection required for damage > $2,000
- All claims: Customer receives confirmation email within 24 hours

STEP 4 — COMMUNICATION
- Update customer within 3 business days of filing
- Provide adjuster contact information
- Set expectations for timeline
- Document all communication in interaction log

SLA TARGETS:
- Acknowledgment: 24 hours
- Initial assessment: 5 business days
- Resolution (simple): 15 business days
- Resolution (complex): 30 business days

title: Customer Risk Signal Definitions and Weights
content:
CUSTOMER RISK SIGNAL DEFINITIONS
================================

The Customer 360 platform uses 7 weighted signals to compute a composite risk score (0.0 to 1.0).

1. RENEWAL PROXIMITY (weight: 0.20)
   How close is the nearest policy renewal?
   - Critical: <= 14 days
   - High: 15-30 days
   - Medium: 31-60 days
   - Low: > 60 days

2. NEGATIVE SENTIMENT (weight: 0.20)
   Count of negative-sentiment interactions in last 90 days.
   Derived from AI sentiment analysis of transcripts and emails.

3. SENTIMENT TREND (weight: 0.15)
   Direction of sentiment change: comparing current 90-day window to prior 90-day window.
   - Worsening: score increasing
   - Stable: no significant change
   - Improving: score decreasing

4. PAYMENT RISK (weight: 0.15)
   Ratio of late + missed payments to total payments.
   Higher ratio = higher risk.

5. COMPLAINT ACTIVITY (weight: 0.10)
   Number of complaint-disposition interactions in last 90 days.

6. CLAIM ACTIVITY (weight: 0.10)
   Number of open (unresolved) claims.

7. ENGAGEMENT DROP (weight: 0.05)
   Decline in interaction frequency compared to historical pattern.

8. CROSS-SELL OPPORTUNITY (weight: 0.05)
   Not a risk signal but a positive indicator. Reduces composite risk when customer has bundling potential.

RISK TIERS:
- Critical: >= 0.75
- High: 0.50 - 0.74
- Medium: 0.25 - 0.49
- Low: < 0.25

title: Data Privacy and Customer Communication Policy
content:
DATA PRIVACY AND CUSTOMER COMMUNICATION POLICY
================================================

RECORDING CONSENT
- All call recordings require explicit verbal consent
- If consent is declined, the call proceeds without recording
- Transcripts from non-consented calls are not processed for AI sentiment analysis
- Consent status is logged per interaction

EMAIL COMMUNICATION
- Customer emails are retained for 7 years per regulatory requirement
- Emails containing PII are stored in encrypted format
- Automated email responses must include opt-out instructions

AI-DERIVED INSIGHTS
- AI sentiment scores are advisory, not deterministic
- Representatives must not share raw AI scores with customers
- Recommendations generated by the NBA engine require human approval
- All AI-assisted decisions are logged in the decision audit trail

CUSTOMER DATA ACCESS
- Service representatives access customer data through the Customer 360 application only
- Direct database access is restricted to data engineers
- Auditors have read-only access to decision logs
- All access is logged and auditable
